blocks.text:
Visit to Iguaçu Falls on the Brazilian side
Today you will discover one of South America’s most impressive natural sights: Iguaçu Falls from the Brazilian side.

The area is home to the famous meeting point of the borders of Brazil, Paraguay and Argentina. There was once a military border post here. As infrastructure and tourism developed, the region became a popular destination for travellers.

The name Iguaçu comes from the language of the Kaingang people and means “great waters”. Formed by the Iguaçu River, the falls comprise numerous cascades surrounded by the tropical forest of Iguaçu National Park.

One of the highlights is the famous Devil’s Throat (Garganta do Diabo). Walkways and viewing platforms offer remarkable views of the powerful cascades and the surrounding forest. The walk gives you different perspectives on the falls and their immense scale.

The Brazilian-side visit is included in the tour price. Optional activities: Great Adventure — USD 125 per person; Bird Park (Parque das Aves) — USD 60 per person.

Great Adventure begins with a route of approximately 6 km along the Yacaratiá Trail through subtropical forest, accompanied by multilingual guides. At Macuco Port, the group boards a boat, travels alongside Martín Island and approaches the cascades and the Devil’s Throat. This optional activity takes place on the Argentine side.

The Bird Park is next to the entrance to the Brazilian national park. It covers 16.5 hectares and is home to more than 800 birds of approximately 200 species, three aviaries and a butterfly pavilion. Among the birds are toucans, scarlet ibises, macaws, jays, thrushes, harpy eagles and owls; reptiles can also be seen. After your visit, you can relax in a restaurant overlooking a lake with flamingos.
